blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Grammar-constrained decoding enables large language models to generate outputs that satisfy formal constraints, but in code and domain-specific language generation, the relevant constraints are not always fully available before decoding and may emerge progressively from new declarations, inferred type information, or runtime analysis feedback. Existing structured-decoding engines efficiently handle fixed, predeclared, or previously seen constraint structures; however, when a first-seen grammar update changes the parser state induced by an already committed prefix, the straightforward solution reconstructs the constraint state under the updated grammar, repeating parsing work already performed over the prefix. We introduce GramDelta, an incremental framework for constrained decoding with append-only runtime grammar updates. GramDelta maintains parse state over the committed prefix and propagates only changes induced by newly added grammar rules through historical dependencies, avoiding prefix replay. It then maps the updated parse state to exact next-token masks via compilation-free factorized projection over shared historical charts, avoiding per-update mask-cache recompilation. GramDelta therefore preserves the result of full reconstruction while making update cost sensitive to the actual impact of a grammar change. Experiments across four model configurations show that GramDelta adds negligible overhead without updates; under sustained runtime grammar evolution, it reduces median first-seen grammar-update latency by 10.7--11.5x and reduces the additional TPOT overhead over unconstrained decoding by 53.1--81.9% relative to the strongest reconstruction baseline. These results enable efficient constrained decoding when constraints progressively emerge and evolve with the generated prefix.

blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Grammar-constrained decoding ( Geng et al., 2023 ; Scholak et al., 2021 ; Dong et al., 2025 ; Hua et al., 2026 ) enables large language models (LLMs) to reliably generate structured outputs that satisfy formal constraints by restricting invalid tokens during decoding.
However, in code and domain-specific language generation, the effective
constraints are not always fully determined before decoding begins and may
instead emerge progressively as generation proceeds ( Li et al., 2026 ) .
A newly generated declaration can introduce identifiers and scopes that did
not previously exist ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) ; type inference can further restrict admissible
expressions ( Mündler et al., 2025 ) ; and static or runtime analyses ( Li et al., 2025 ) can determine which fields, APIs, or program actions are valid for the current partial program.
The common feature of these settings is that the information determining valid continuations becomes available only as the generation context is established.

blocks.en: 2.2 Runtime Grammar Evolution and State Maintenance
blocks.zh: 2.2 运行时间语法演变和国家维护

blocks.en:
Recent constrained-decoding systems support dynamic structure at several
levels. llguidance uses an Earley recognizer together with a derivative-based lexer
and tokenizer-trie traversal to compute token masks for a supplied grammar ( Guidance AI, 2025 ) .
XGrammar-2 targets dynamic agentic workloads: TagDispatch switches among
grammar components during generation, while cross-grammar caching,
adaptive Earley token-mask caching, and just-in-time compilation reuse work
across related structures ( Li et al., 2026 ) .
Decode-Time Grammars provide a complementary form of dynamism by instantiating
grammar fragments from an evolving runtime environment Γ \Gamma , allowing the
constraint applied to later regions to depend on declarations already
generated ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) .
Other code-generation methods similarly derive context-sensitive constraints
from type, scope, or program state ( Mündler et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ) .
Collectively, these methods make generation-time constraints more efficient to
construct, select, or execute.

We compare GramDelta against internal and external baselines:

applies the grammar delta directly to its persistent request-local recognizer
state.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced GramDelta, an incremental framework for
constrained decoding under append-only runtime grammar
updates. By combining historical dependency localization,
semi-naive Earley closure, and exact factorized token
projection, GramDelta maintains the same parser state and
next-token mask as full reconstruction without replaying
the committed prefix. Its benefits depend on update locality:
broad changes may favor reconstruction, while supporting
deletions and replacements requires provenance-aware
retraction.
